newsitem.title: GERMANY: Schmidhuber-EMU members must show yrs of stability.
newsitem.headline: Schmidhuber-EMU members must show yrs of stability.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Peter Schmidhuber said on Friday that nations seeking to join Europe's planned monetary union must show they have pursued stability-oriented policies in past years and that they have reached the required level of lasting convergence.
This was important for the success of the single currency, or euro, Schmidhuber said in a speech.
"Hectic" attempts to meet the deficit criteria were causing only the appearance of convergence, and that appearance was being enhanced by speculation in the capital markets, Schmidhuber said.
Schmidhuber said that if bond yields of a country fall because capital markets expect it to join EMU that has nothing to do with convergence, "but is the result of speculative investment decisions."
He also said that while the stability pact on ensuring lasting fiscal discipline after monetary union was important, its effect was limited if there was a dispute.
"One-off shows of strength in budget policy already carry the seeds of a fall back into fiscal laxity," Schmidhuber said.
"Cooking the books and creative accounting must be prevented as far as possible."

"For a successful start of the euro it is important that the currency union only begins with those countries which can prove they have pursued stability policies in past years and have reached the required degree of lasting convergence."
Accepting countries which had failed to convince the European public or financial markets that they were stability-oriented would burden monetary union from the start, Schmidhuber said.
He said: "From my point of view it is problematic when individual member states turn joining currency union from the start into a matter of national prestige.
"Here all participants should show restraint because this could otherwise lead to a dangerous constellation."
